text:
sam: hi all — finishing up my dev bootstrap and hit a couple annoyances. mac M1 setup was smooth but I'm on Ubuntu 22.04 WSL2 and running into TLS/proxy issues when pulling docker images and when asdf tries to fetch nodejs. any tips?

alice: welcome! can you paste the exact errors?

sam: for docker: 
```
$ docker pull registry.redwood.internal/base:latest
Error response from daemon: Get \"https://registry.redwood.internal/v2/\": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

sam: and for asdf/nodejs plugin: 
```
$ asdf plugin-add nodejs
gpg: failed to start agent
gpg: can't connect to the agent: IPC connect call failed
```

matt: two likely separate things — corporate TLS intercept + missing gpg agent / pinentry in WSL. We lock down images behind our internal registry so you'll need the corp CA in your distro trust chain.

matt: infra path: add the CA to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and run `sudo update-ca-certificates`. For WSL, also make sure Docker Desktop (if you're using it) trusts that cert.

sam: ok trying that. quick question — where do I fetch the CA? internal wiki has a blob but it was behind SSO. @devops any quick public endpoint?

devops: uploaded the current corp-root.crt to the team s3 bucket. link: https://s3.redwood/internal/certs/corp-root.crt (requires okta). If you can't access, DM me and I'll drop it in a thread. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks. after adding CA, docker pull changed to TLS handshake but now I get auth denied (401) when pulling a private image.

alice: you need to `docker login registry.redwood.internal` using your SSO token. We use the `redwood-cli auth login` flow which exchanges OKTA cookies. Try: `redwood-cli login && docker login registry.redwood.internal -u $(redwood-cli docker-username) -p $(redwood-cli docker-token)`

sam: that worked. back to gpg/asdf: `gpg: failed to start agent` persists. I installed `gnupg2` and `pinentry-curses` but asdf still can't fetch keys for nodejs releases.

matt: in WSL sometimes gpg needs `gpg-agent` running or a proper pinentry. run `gpgconf --launch gpg-agent` then `echo test | gpg --clearsign` to confirm. Also ensure `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` in your shell rc.

sam: tried that — `gpg: signing failed: Inappropriate ioctl for device`

matt: oh that's the tty issue in WSL. Add `export GPG_TTY=/dev/tty` in your `~/.bashrc` or `~/.profile`, and disable pinentry interactive by adding to `~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf`: `pinentry-program /usr/bin/pinentry-curses` and `allow-loopback-pinentry`. Then restart the agent: `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent && gpgconf --launch gpg-agent`.

sam: made the changes, asdf nodejs plugin now downloads keys but fails at `node-pre-gyp` build step when installing node. error: `node: symbol lookup error: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6: undefined symbol: GLIBCXX_3.4.29`

alice: that usually means mismatched libstdc++ (older distro libs vs newer prebuilt binaries). For WSL folks we recommend installing Node via binary tarballs only after installing compatibility libs, or use `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0 --use-system-libc` (we have a wrapper script). Which asdf/nodejs version are you using?

sam: asdf 0.11.3 and nodejs plugin 0.9.0.

matt: try `sudo apt install libstdc++6` (maybe you're on an older runtime inside WSL distro). If that still fails, use the distro package `apt install nodejs` as a fallback, then `asdf` can be told to shim it. But we prefer a consistent asdf-managed runtime — I'll paste our internal helper script.

matt: ```bash
# quick helper (internal)
export NODEJS_SHA_VERIFY=false
asdf install nodejs 18.16.0
```
note: turning off sha verify is NOT ideal; infra only allows it for initial bootstrap. After you get going, we'll help you install proper toolchain.

sam: used the helper and node installed. last thing — direnv + .envrc complains about `permission denied` when loading `.envrc` after I added `layout python` and `source_up` lines.

alice: run `direnv allow` from the project dir. If CI/pre-commit expects automatic allow, we have a repo `.envrc` whitelist in the org. Also ensure `eval "$(direnv hook bash)"` is in your shell rc.

sam: yep I had missed the hook. now everything's green. Thanks for the quick help! Quick follow-ups: can someone point me to the WSL recommended distro image and the onboarding checklist?

devops: onboarding checklist: https://wiki.redwood/dev-onboarding (includes recommended WSL2 distro image link + common gotchas). Also ping `#eng-infra` if you want us to do a short pair session to get you fully production-ready.

sam: awesome — appreciate it. cc @alice @matt for any follow-up. :party:

infra-bot: Note: ticket INF-4821 created to track improving WSL onboarding docs and a one-click cert distribution for new-hires (assigned to devops).
